reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR introduces a machine-checkable “certificate” data model to carry empirical/structural claims (with CIDs), along with CBOR serialization and protocol attestation checks, and begins migrating scoring/graph plumbing toward a fixed-point `ScoreQ` representation. **Changes:** - Add `transformerless::certificate` with CID computation/verification, Gate K attestation checks, and CBOR encode/decode. - Add `transformerless::score_q::ScoreQ` (Q16.16 fixed-point) and thread a `ScoreQ` field into `TransitionGraph::Edge`. - Add new unit tests for `ScoreQ` behavior and certificate CID/CBOR/attestation behavior, plus add `ciborium` dependency. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 7 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/score_q_test.rs | Adds tests for `ScoreQ` conversion precision, saturating arithmetic, and descriptor decoding. | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/certificate_test.rs | Adds tests for certificate CID verification, CBOR roundtrip, and attestation failure cases. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/transitions.rs | Extends `Edge` to carry a `ScoreQ` and adds an `add_edge_with_score` constructor path. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/score_q.rs | Introduces the `ScoreQ` fixed-point type and `StorageDescriptor` decoding. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/mod.rs | Exposes `ScoreQ` (and `Certificate` for non-wasm targets) and registers new modules. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/certificate.rs | Implements the certificate schema, CID computation/verification, CBOR serialization, and attestation validation. | | crates/uor-r4-core/Cargo.toml | Adds `ciborium` dependency to support CBOR serialization. | | Cargo.lock | Locks `ciborium` and its transitive dependencies. |

review_comments.body: `ScoreQ::from_logprob` takes an `f32`, but these literals default to `f64`, which will fail to compile due to a type mismatch. Add `f32` suffixes (or cast) to the literals.

`weight` is a `u32`, but `weight as i32` can wrap for values > `i32::MAX`, producing a negative raw `ScoreQ` and silently corrupting the score. Clamp before converting (or require callers to provide an explicit `ScoreQ`).

`from_logprob` quantizes via `as i32`, which truncates toward zero and introduces a systematic bias. Rounding to the nearest fixed-point value typically yields better and symmetric quantization error.

`StorageDescriptor::decode` uses `wrapping_shl`/`wrapping_shr`, so large shifts or overflow will wrap the value, which can break monotonicity and yield nonsensical decoded scores. Prefer checked shifts and saturate/clamp on overflow.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+//! Machine-checkable Certificate schema for empirical and structural claims
+//! emitted by the R4 holographic graph compiler.
+
+use blake3::Hasher;
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub enum ClaimKind {
+    Structural,
+    Empirical,
+    Performance,
+    Safety,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct EmpiricalClaim {
+    pub name: String,
+    pub sample_size: u64,
+    pub metric_value: f64,
+    pub confidence_interval_95: (f64, f64),
+    pub slice_label: String,
+    pub claim_kind: ClaimKind,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
+pub struct ProtocolAttestation {
+    pub deterministic_canonical_mode: bool,
+    pub zero_allocation_verified: bool,
+    pub no_multiply_verified: bool,
+    pub theorem_7_reverse_index_verified: bool,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct Certificate {
+    pub version: u32,
+    pub certificate_cid: String,
+    pub source_cid: String,
+    pub corpus_cid: String,
+    pub graph_cid: String,
+    pub metric_cid: String,
+    pub op_cid: String,
+    pub benchmark_cid: String,
+    pub claims: Vec<EmpiricalClaim>,
+    pub attestation: ProtocolAttestation,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum CertificateError {
+    SerializationError(String),
+    DeserializationError(String),
+    CidMismatch { expected: String, actual: String },
+    AttestationFailed(String),
+}
+
+impl Certificate {
+    pub fn new(
+        source_cid: impl Into<String>,
+        corpus_cid: impl Into<String>,
+        graph_cid: impl Into<String>,
+        metric_cid: impl Into<String>,
+        op_cid: impl Into<String>,
+        benchmark_cid: impl Into<String>,
+        claims: Vec<EmpiricalClaim>,
+        attestation: ProtocolAttestation,
+    ) -> Self {
+        let mut cert = Certificate {
+            version: 1,
+            certificate_cid: String::new(),
+            source_cid: source_cid.into(),
+            corpus_cid: corpus_cid.into(),
+            graph_cid: graph_cid.into(),
+            metric_cid: metric_cid.into(),
+            op_cid: op_cid.into(),
+            benchmark_cid: benchmark_cid.into(),
+            claims,
+            attestation,
+        };
+        cert.certificate_cid = cert.compute_cid();
+        cert
+    }
+
+    /// Compute self-referential BLAKE3 CID (hex format) over certificate content.
+    pub fn compute_cid(&self) -> String {
+        let mut clone = self.clone();
+        clone.certificate_cid.clear();
+        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&clone).unwrap_or_default();
+        let mut hasher = Hasher::new();
+        hasher.update(&bytes);
+        format!("kappa:blake3:{}", hasher.finalize().to_hex())
+    }
review_comments.body: The PR/issue describe a CBOR-serialized, canonical certificate, but `compute_cid` currently hashes `serde_json` output and also silently falls back to empty bytes on serialization error (`unwrap_or_default`). That makes the CID depend on JSON formatting and can incorrectly “verify” when serialization fails. Compute the CID over CBOR bytes and fail fast on serialization errors.
`verify_attestation` never checks `deterministic_canonical_mode`, so an attestation can pass even when the canonical-mode requirement is explicitly marked false.
